description: Hi everyone! We are Team Neutron is a multidisciplinary team bridging life sciences, medicine, mechatronics engineering, and AI development. Driven by a passion for STEM education and space exploration, we combine scientific rigor, mathematical modeling, and AI-driven prototyping to build high-impact, interactive learning experiences.
summary:
We developed NEUTRÓN, an interactive, gamified, web-based space simulator designed for young students to explore the Moon and Mars while training like real astronauts. The platform addresses the challenge of making space science more accessible through active learning: instead of passively consuming theory, users take on critical roles, make real-time decisions, and resolve emergencies by managing vital resources—such as oxygen, energy, food, and health—all supported by open-source NASA data and guided instruction. This project is significant because it democratizes access to space exploration, demonstrating that a lack of interest among young people is not due to a lack of talent, but rather a lack of hands-on opportunities. Through gamification, NEUTRÓN strengthens critical thinking, collaborative work, and meaningful learning, creating a multiplier effect that sparks an early interest in STEM careers.Neutrón is for you; we aim to decentralize space sciences.

TALKING ABOUT INNOVATION...

Our vision for the next two years is for Neutrón to be more than just a platform—to become a community of young people who have discovered that they, too, can play a part in the future of space exploration.
details:
NEUTRÓN is a gamified web-based simulator in which young students train as astronauts on missions to the "Artemis" Lunar Base and the "Ares" Mars Base. Guided by LUNA an online AI users select their destination, space weather conditions, and role (Life Support Systems, Energy and Shielding, Food Supplies, or Medical Officer/Commander) to resolve scientific emergencies across six stages. In real time, they must balance oxygen, energy, food, and health, guided by immediate visual feedback.The platform transforms complex concepts from physics, biology, and space medicine into hands-on experiences for digital natives, fostering critical thinking, collaborative work, and interest in STEM fields. To ensure scientific rigor, we incorporate open data from NASA and partner agencies, covering areas such as cartography and missions (Moon/Mars Trek, PDS, HiRISE, NSSDC, and Landsat), physics and space weather (PSI, SPHEREx, AppEEARS, MODIS/VIIRS, and Chandra), and space health (OSDR and the Human Research Program).

Their creativity lies in transforming the screen into a living space laboratory, designed with youth accessibility in mind and demonstrating that a lack of scientific interest stems from a lack of practical opportunities, not a lack of talent.
